name: expect_subset
title: Reports the matching check through the active test backend

origin.description: Reports the matching check through the active test backend. A failure stops with the check message.
origin.usage: expect_subset(x, choices, empty.ok = TRUE, fmatch = FALSE, info = NULL, label = vname(x))

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Value under test. A Python int is an R integer and a Python float is an R double.

arguments.name: fmatch
arguments.text: Ignored. Matching uses Python's base match.

arguments.name: info
arguments.text: Extra text added when an expectation fails.

arguments.name: label
arguments.text: Name used in the expectation message.

origin.details: Reports the matching check through the active test backend. A failure stops with the check message.
origin.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check stops.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(checkmate))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tibble))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(R6))
obj <- R6Class("Bar", public = list(a = 5), private = list(b = 42))$new()
fn <- function(x) x
print(expect_subset("a", letters))

translation.description: Reports the matching check through the active test backend. A failure stops with the check message.
translation.usage: expect_subset(x, choices, empty_ok=True, fmatch=False, info=None, label=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Value under test. A Python int is an R integer and a Python float is an R double.

arguments.name: empty_ok
arguments.text: When false, an empty value fails the check.

arguments.name: fmatch
arguments.text: Ignored. Matching uses Python's base match.

arguments.name: info
arguments.text: Extra text added when an expectation fails.

arguments.name: label
arguments.text: Name used in the expectation message.

translation.details: Reports the matching check through the active test backend. A failure stops with the check message.
translation.value: The value when the check passes. An expectation failure raises CheckError.
translation.example:
from checkmate import *

letters = list('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz')

def fn(x):
    return x

obj = R6('Bar', public={'a': 5}, private={'b': 42})
from datetime import date as D
DAY = (D(2020, 1, 2) - D(1970, 1, 1)).days

print(expect_subset("a", letters))
